panels.title: Metrics Server Deployment Health (Kubernetes)
panels.description: Is the metrics-server workload itself healthy at the Kubernetes level - independent of whether it is successfully talking to the WEKA API. Sourced from kube-state-metrics (job="kube-state-metrics").

panels.title: Desired Replicas
panels.description: From kube-state-metrics for the metrics-server Deployment(s) matched by $namespace/$deployment.

panels.title: Available Replicas
panels.description: From kube-state-metrics for the metrics-server Deployment(s) matched by $namespace/$deployment.

panels.title: Unavailable Replicas
panels.description: From kube-state-metrics for the metrics-server Deployment(s) matched by $namespace/$deployment.

panels.title: Updated Replicas
panels.description: From kube-state-metrics for the metrics-server Deployment(s) matched by $namespace/$deployment.

panels.title: Rollout: updated < desired
panels.description: 1 while the Deployment is mid-rollout (fewer replicas updated to the latest spec than desired).

panels.title: Rollout: generation lagging
panels.description: 1 when the controller has not yet observed the latest Deployment spec change (observedGeneration < metadata.generation) - another sign a rollout is in flight or stuck.

panels.title: Container restarts (last 1h)
panels.description: Per pod/container restart count over a trailing 1h window. Any non-zero value warrants a look at `kubectl describe pod` / previous logs.

panels.title: CrashLoopBackOff
panels.description: A series appears here only while a container is actively in CrashLoopBackOff. No data/empty panel means none are - that is the healthy state, not a broken query.

panels.title: Containers Not Ready
panels.description: This Deployment intentionally ships with NO readinessProbe (PR #740), so a container's ready state here just tracks the container being started, not real request-serving health, and cannot distinguish the active leader from standby replicas. See the Leader identity panel to find who is actually serving. A non-zero count still means a container failed to start (e.g. crash, image pull), which IS a fault.

panels.title: Containers OOMKilled (last terminated reason)
panels.description: Count of containers whose most recent termination was an OOM kill. Sticky until the container is next terminated for a different reason.

panels.title: Leader identity (kube_lease_owner)
panels.description: Who currently holds each CSI lease in the metrics-server namespace(s): csi.weka.io-metricsserver-leader is the metrics-server's own leader-election lease; csi.weka.io-controller-leader (when the plugin controller shares the namespace) is the CSI controller's lease. PR #739 fixed a bug where a metrics-server pod could steal the controller's lease, hanging provisioning while every pod still looked Running - if lease_holder for the controller lease is ever a metrics-server pod name, that bug has recurred.

panels.title: Pod age
panels.description: Time since each pod started. A pod age that resets unexpectedly (without a corresponding rollout) indicates an unplanned restart.

panels.title: Image / version per pod
panels.description: Per-pod running image/tag. During a rolling update this will legitimately show old and new versions side by side; if it stays mixed long after a rollout should have finished, check the Replicas panels above for a stuck rollout.

panels.title: Sum of URL requests over time
PersistentVolumes reporting capacity
panels.description: How many volumes produced a fresh capacity reading inside the window. "From PV spec" comes from the Kubernetes PersistentVolume object and should equal the number of valid PVs at all times. The "From WEKA Stats" series come from the WEKA API and carry the timestamp of their own measurement, so each volume yields roughly one sample per quotaCacheValiditySeconds - a window at or below that value undercounts, and the series appears to lose volumes periodically.

list.label: Max age of values
list.name: value_max_age
list.description: Freshness window for capacity readings. Must be larger than the metrics server's quotaCacheValiditySeconds (chart default 300s), or volumes that have not been re-fetched yet drop out and the count sawtooths.

list.label: monitorserver pod
list.name: pod
list.description: Metrics server pods. Defaults to All on purpose: the collector is leader-elected, so a standby publishes no WEKA API or fetch metrics and selecting one shows empty panels.

list.label: Metrics server namespace
list.name: namespace
list.description: Namespace(s) hosting the metrics-server Deployment. Regex default matches both the standalone csi-metricsserver chart and the plugin chart's optional metricsServer.enabled Deployment under any Helm release name, since both always name the Deployment '<release>-metrics-server'.

list.label: Metrics server deployment
list.name: deployment
list.description: Deployment name(s) of the metrics server, scoped to $namespace. The default regex '.*-metrics-server' matches any release name for either chart shape and does NOT match the unrelated built-in Kubernetes 'metrics-server' Deployment in kube-system (whose name has no '-metrics-server' suffix).
